title: International residency decision log and evidence guide
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:

This page defines the decision logging, technical controls, and evidence packaging requirements for cross-border and international data residency decisions. It is intended for Security, Legal, Data Governance, Infra, and SRE teams who must decide where inference traces, prompts, model artifacts, and customer data may reside, how to implement routing and isolation, and how to collect audit evidence for compliance reviews.

Goals:
- Provide a clear, auditable decision record format for residency choices.
- Define required evidence artifacts and retention windows per artifact type.
- Prescribe technical controls (RBAC, KMS, network isolation, audit logging) to enforce residency.
- Describe the incident / legal-hold process and evidence handoff for cross-border events.

Scope:
- This guide covers decisions affecting: hosted API requests, Dedicated pools, Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), model artifacts, prefix/KV caches, and telemetry containing PII or customer identifiers.
- Not covered: export-control decisions for cryptographic software (handled by Legal export controls).

Decision record template (required for every residency change):
1) Decision ID: residency-yyyy-mm-dd-<shortid>
2) Summary: one-paragraph rationale (product need, customer requirement, legal trigger).
3) Impacted assets: list service names, e.g. policy-orch, inference-gateway, audit-ingest, evidence-archiver, residency-decisions-db.
4) Proposed configuration: region routing policy, allowed regions, failover behavior.
5) Evidence artifacts to collect (table below).
6) Stakeholders and approvals: Data Governance, Security, Legal, Product, Infra owners.
7) Rollout plan and rollback criteria.
8) Retention schedule (see retention matrix).
9) Link to related ADR or runbook.

Required approvals and SLA for sign-off:
- Technical review (Infra): 3 business days.
- Legal/compliance review: 5 business days.
- Final security approval: 2 business days after others.
Note: emergency changes require documented emergency exception and must be reconciled into a full decision record within 48 hours.

Retention and evidence matrix (authoritative):
| Artifact type                       | Example path / service                 | Minimum retention | Owner team       |
|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------:|------------------|
| Audit ingestion stream events       | audit-ingest/streams/*                 | 7 years           | security         |
| Auth/entitlement changes (RBAC)     | rbac-audit/changes/*                   | 7 years           | security         |
| Residency decision record           | residency-decisions-db                 | 10 years          | data-governance  |
| Snapshot of configuration (prod)    | infra-config/prod/<service>/snapshot   | 5 years           | infra            |
| Evidence bundle (for audits)        | evidence-bucket/<decision-id>/*.zip    | 10 years          | security         |
| Model artifact provenance metadata   | model-catalog/provenance/*             | 7 years           | applied-ml       |
| Key usage logs (KMS/HSM)            | redwood-kms/key-usage/*                | 3 years           | security         |
| Legal hold markers                   | legal-hold/index                       | until released    | legal            |

Technical controls (mandatory):
- RBAC: All residency decisions must be implemented with least-privilege entitlements. Use service identities with scoped roles: residency-controller, residency-viewer, residency-approver. JIT access for approvers is required for emergency changes. See /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-sandboxing-playbook-for-model-serving-2026 for patterns.
- Audit logging: All configuration changes must create an immutable audit event in audit-ingest with fields: event_id, actor, action, target, before, after, decision_id. Audit-ingest has an SLA: 99.9% ingestion success within 1 minute.
- KMS/HSM: Any residency-bound customer keys must be bound to a region-specific KMS key. redwood-kms must emit key_usage events to audit-ingest.
- Network controls: VPC-level egress policies and private-link routing controls must match residency policy. For Private deployments we require a signed network attestation before acceptance.

Evidence artifacts (detailed):
- Decision record (JSON): residency decisions must be written to residency-decisions-db and include the following fields: decision_id, created_by, approvers, approved_at, impacted_services, allowed_regions, rollback_criteria, evidence_bundle_path. Example metadata (JSON snippet):
{
  "decision_id": "residency-2026-01-12-7c4f",
  "created_by": "m.patel@redwood.ai",
  "approvers": ["s.legal@redwood.ai", "e.brooks@redwood.ai"],
  "allowed_regions": ["us-west-2", "eu-west-1"]
}
- Audit event package: bundle of audit-ingest records that show the change, entitlement checks, routing updates, and KMS key assignments. The package must include checksums (SHA256) and a manifest file.
- Configuration snapshot: Terraform/Helm snapshots with diff against previous snapshot and a short runbook describing how the config enforces residency.
- Access evidence: list of accounts granted new entitlements and the justification notes captured in the entitlement ticket.

Packaging and chain-of-custody:
- Evidence bundles must be created by the evidence-archiver service running in the same region as the primary residency asset.
- Bundle naming convention: evidence-bundle-<decision_id>-<YYYYMMDD>-<sha256>.zip
- Each bundle must contain a manifest.json and be signed with the redwood-evidence signing key (HSM-stored).
- Chain-of-custody log: append-only ledger entry in evidence-ledger with fields: bundle_name, created_at, created_by, signer, checksum, storage_path.

Retention and purging process:
1) Retention windows are enforced by retention-indexer.
2) For artifacts with >3 year retention, generate archival copies into long-term object storage (cold-evidence) and write an archival proof record to residency-decisions-db.
3) Purge job must keep an immutable proof-of-purge record (signed) for at least 90 days after purge.

Cross-border incident playbook (high level):
1) Detection: if telemetry indicates unauthorized replication to an out-of-scope region, open an incident using the tag: incident:residency-cross-border and notify Security, Legal, Data Governance.
2) Containment: run the immediate containment CLI (requires residency-approver):
   - curl -X POST https://platform-api/internal/residency/actions/freeze-replication -d '{"decision_id":"<id>","scope":"service:<svc>"}' 
   - or use: redwoodctl residency freeze --service <svc> --decision <decision_id>
3) Evidence preservation:
   - Create a legal-hold marker in legal-hold/index (Legal).
   - Trigger evidence-archiver to create a time-stamped bundle (evidence-bundle-<id>-<ts>.zip).
   - Lock related audit partitions and disable retention purging for affected partitions.
4) Investigation: Security will collect audit-ingest partitions, RBAC change events, KMS key-usage logs, and network flow logs. Legal will assess whether additional notification is required.
5) Remediation and post-incident decision: update residency decision record with findings and mitigation steps, include re-approval if a new allowed region is needed.

Change rollout and testing steps (minimum required):
1) Draft decision in residency-decisions-db (dev).
2) Unit tests: static checks validating no global-allow rules are present.
3) Staging canary: apply policy to a canary service in staging region with synthetic traffic for 72h.
4) Preflight: run residency-policy-scan and evidence-collection smoke test.
5) Prod rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24–72 hours with continuous monitoring of routing failures and P50/P99 latency.
6) Post-rollout: confirm evidence bundle was generated, manifest validated, and retention index updated.

Monitoring and alerts (examples):
- Alert: residency-policy-apply-failure (S1) — threshold: >5% failed writes to policy-orch in 5m. Pager to Infra and Security.
- Alert: audit-ingest-delay (S2) — threshold: >1 minute median ingestion latency over 5m. Pager to Observability.
- Alert: cross-region-replica-detected (S1) — any replication event to non-allowed region. Pager to Security and Legal.

RBAC checklist for implementers:
- Confirm service identities are scoped; do not use high-privilege admin tokens.
- Use timebound entitlements for migration or emergency scenarios.
- Ensure entitlement events are captured and routed to audit-ingest with actor identity.

Operational examples and commands:
- Create decision (CLI):
  redwoodctl residency create --title "EU-only model serving for AcmeCorp" --allowed-regions eu-west-1 --approvers s.legal@redwood.ai,e.brooks@redwood.ai --output json > decision.json
- Freeze replication (API):
  curl -X POST "https://platform-api/internal/residency/actions/freeze-replication" 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","decision_id":"residency-2026-01-12-7c4f"}'

Appendix A — Quick evidence manifest schema (manifest.json inside bundle):
{
  "bundle_name": "evidence-bundle-residency-2026-01-12-7c4f-20260112-abc123.zip",
  "decision_id": "residency-2026-01-12-7c4f",
  "created_at": "2026-01-12T15:22:00Z",
  "files": ["audit_events.ndjson","config_snapshot.tar.gz","kms_key_usage.log"],
  "signer": "redwood-evidence-hsm-01",
  "checksum_sha256": "<sha256>"
}

Notes and non-normative guidance:
- When in doubt, default to stricter residency and longer evidence retention for regulated customers.
- This guide does not replace legal counsel — always include Legal for jurisdictional questions.
